name: Osteoblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for osteoblastoma

criteria.description: Presence of interlacing trabeculae of woven bone lined by prominent osteoblasts with vascularized connective tissue stroma
Radiographic appearance of an expansile, well-demarcated osteolytic lesion with variable mineralization, typically >2 cm in size
Localized dull aching pain often unresponsive to NSAIDs and swelling at the affected site

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation combined with characteristic radiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from osteoid osteoma and osteosarcoma is critical due to overlapping features.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized dull aching bone pain unresponsive to NSAIDs
searchTerms: bone ache not helped by painkillers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable bony swelling at the lesion site

common.symptomName: Restricted range of motion if lesion is near a joint
Mild local warmth over the lesion

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to spinal involvement (e.g., radiculopathy)

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk near affected area

occasional.symptomName: Mild systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: slight systemic symptoms like mild fever

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits from spinal cord compression
searchTerms: weakness due to spinal cord squeezing
loss of sensation from spinal compression

laboratory: Typically normal laboratory values; inflammatory markers usually not elevated
imaging: X-ray: Expansile, radiolucent lesion >2 cm with variable mineralization
CT scan: Detailed cortical involvement and nidus visualization
MRI: Soft tissue extension and marrow edema assessment
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence

distinguishingFeatures: Less expansile and less aggressive radiographic appearance
Malignant histological features with atypia and mitotic figures

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord or nerve root compression
Unrelenting pain not responding to standard analgesics
references: Dorfman HD, Czerniak B. Bone Cancers. Cancer. 1995;75(1 Suppl):203-210.
Kransdorf MJ, Sweet DE. Osteoblastoma. Radiographics. 1994;14(4):837-857.
